extracted.intended_audience: concerned members of the public and environmental advocates (Earthjustice supporters) who will submit public comments or contact elected officials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public on why and how to submit comments during federal rulemaking and to elected officials to influence decisions and build the administrative record used in litigation. Focused on environmental rulemaking and grassroots advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put a face and a name on an issue
rubrics_metrics.description: When you contact your elected official, you’re putting a face and a name on an issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify yourself and your relationship to the community or issue so officials see who they represent. (The page points readers to tools to find local, state, and federal elected officials.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Include your specific experiences, knowledge, and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Your specific experiences, knowledge, and voice are crucial to add to the Administrative Record through the comment periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personal stories, lived experience, or local knowledge to supplement technical/legal submissions; those personal accounts provide context and support for agency and court consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments during official comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments are collected at various points throughout the federal government’s rulemaking process, including when a regulation is proposed and finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be submitted within the published comment period to become part of the Administrative Record and to be considered by the agency; action alerts list deadlines (e.g., '27 Days Remain').

rubrics_metrics.name: Make comments part of the Administrative Record (support litigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: These comments become part of the official, legal public record — the 'Administrative Record.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts can only review documents in the Administrative Record when judging agency actions; well-documented public comments can provide factual and legal bases for lawsuits challenging harmful agency decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level the playing field against industry lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Elected officials pay attention when they see that we are paying attention. They may be hearing from industry lobbyists left and right, but hearing the stories of their constituents — that’s your power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comments and direct contact to show broad constituent concern and counterbalance industry influence; emphasize community values and democratic accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complement technical/legal comments with personal submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout each of the public comment periods we alert you to, Earthjustice’s attorneys are researching and writing in-depth, technical comments to submit — detailing how the regulation could and should be stronger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the distinction: legal/technical comments (prepared by attorneys or experts) are important for legal arguments, while public personal comments add lived experience and local impacts. Both types strengthen the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass participation matters — volume influences outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: When the public responds with a huge outpouring of support for environmental protections, these individual messages collectively undercut politicians' attempts to claim otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage wide participation and sharing to increase the number of comments; a large number of individualized comments can change perceptions and influence agency and political responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe concrete harms, risks, and community impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments in the Bristol Bay example highlight contamination risks, mitigation failures, threats to fisheries, and the pricelessness of a pristine watershed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about potential environmental, health, or economic harms and how proposed actions would affect local communities or resources; concrete examples are more persuasive than vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite credible studies or professional experience when available
rubrics_metrics.description: One commenter referenced 'a recent study by the University of Washington' and another identified themselves as a 'retired Deputy Director' with first-hand knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you can, cite reputable studies, data, or your professional credentials to bolster factual claims; include sources or describe relevant expertise to strengthen the comment’s weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the legal framework (NEPA, APA) that requires justification of agency actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many laws (like NEPA and the APA) require our government to ask the public to weigh in before agencies adopt or change regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness of statutory requirements can inform comments (e.g., pointing out procedural or substantive legal deficiencies); mention relevant legal standards if you are raising procedural or legal objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay informed and act promptly (use alerts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay informed by text: take action and make an impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign up for action alerts and timely notifications so you can respond quickly to comment opportunities and meet deadlines; the site’s action items often include countdowns to closing dates.
